summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science degree: asymptotic analysis, discrete mathematics (sets, functions, combinatorial counting, induction, basic modular arithmetic and number theory such as primes, gcd and the Euclidean algorithm), recursion and elementary algorithms (sorting, stacks, divide and conquer), basic Turing machines with several tapes, and the first-year mathematics that goes with it: single-variable calculus (limits, convergence of sequences and series, basic integrals, geometric series), matrices and vectors, polynomials and complex numbers. The reader has not met the discrete Fourier transform or the FFT, abstract algebra beyond modular arithmetic (rings, quotient rings, algebra isomorphisms, cyclic-group structure), Gaussian integers, number-theoretic results on the density of primes, or any integer-multiplication algorithm faster than the schoolbook method.

known.name: Logarithms and exponentials
known.gloss: The base-2 and natural logarithms and their identities, used for bit lengths, the lg n notation, and for treating exponents like (lg n)^{1-kappa} or 2^{-p} as growing or shrinking functions.

known.name: Floor, ceiling and rounding
known.gloss: The functions giving the greatest integer at most x, the least integer at least x, and the nearest integer to x, used for lengths such as ceil(log2 n) and for rounding computed values to integers.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: An integer written as a string of digits in radix 2 (or any radix b) with the leftmost digit most significant, so val(x) = sum x_i 2^{n-i}, with padding by leading zeros to a fixed length.

known.name: Schoolbook arithmetic and carries
known.gloss: The elementary algorithms for adding and multiplying integers digit by digit with carries, taking linear time for addition and quadratic time for multiplication.

known.name: Bitwise operations and XOR
known.gloss: Logical operations on bits, in particular exclusive or, which is addition modulo 2 and is its own inverse.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and residues
known.gloss: Arithmetic on remainders modulo m, where a is congruent to b mod m when m divides a-b, with addition, multiplication and inverses of numbers coprime to m.

known.name: Primes, divisibility and coprimality
known.gloss: Divisibility of integers, prime numbers, the gcd and the Euclidean algorithm (including its extended form giving modular inverses), and the meaning of coprime and pairwise coprime integers.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: The complex numbers w with w^t = 1, namely e^{2 pi i k/t}, which are the unit-modulus complex numbers whose powers cycle with period t.

known.name: Complex modulus, conjugate and triangle inequality
aliases: absolute value of a complex number
known.gloss: The modulus |z| = sqrt(a^2+b^2) of a complex number, its real and imaginary parts, and the inequality |u+v| <= |u|+|v| used to bound sums of errors.

known.name: Max norm and error bounds
known.gloss: The norm of a vector as its largest coordinate in absolute value, used to state that every coordinate of a computed array is within a stated error of the true one.

known.name: Little-o, big-Omega and Theta notation
known.gloss: The companions of big-O notation: f = o(g) when f/g tends to 0, f = Omega(g) for a lower bound, and Theta for matching upper and lower bounds.

known.name: Series and exponential decay estimates
known.gloss: Sums of geometric series and similar convergent series, and the fact that quantities like 2^{-p} are negligible against any fixed polynomial in the relevant size, used to sum recursive costs and bound errors.

known.name: Recurrences and recursion
known.gloss: Defining a procedure by calls to itself on smaller inputs, analyzing its cost by a recurrence such as F_k <= a F_{k-1} + c, and proving bounds by induction.

known.name: Sorting and stacks
known.gloss: Rearranging records into a prescribed order by comparison or by key, and the stack data structure with push and pop, used for depth-first recursion.

known.name: Sets, subsets and counting
known.gloss: Finite sets, subsets of a given size, intersections, Cartesian products of sets, binomial coefficients and the indicator (0/1) vector of a subset.

known.name: Permutations and bijections
known.gloss: A bijective rearrangement of a finite index set, its inverse, and the corresponding permutation matrix that reorders the entries of a list.

known.name: Lexicographic order and mixed-radix indices
known.gloss: Ordering tuples by comparing coordinates left to right, and storing a multidimensional array as a flat list so that a tuple (i_1,...,i_d) is at position sum i_j times the product of later axis lengths.

known.name: Matrices, matrix-vector products and inverses
known.gloss: Rectangular arrays of numbers acting on vectors by multiplication, with the identity, inverses of invertible matrices, and diagonal and triangular matrices.

known.name: Kronecker product of matrices
known.gloss: The block matrix A (x) B formed from two matrices, which acts on tensor-product index sets and satisfies (A (x) B)(C (x) D) = AC (x) BD.

known.name: Hadamard matrix and the 2x2 butterfly matrix
known.gloss: The 2x2 matrix with rows (1,1) and (1,-1) (up to scaling), whose tensor powers act on bit-indexed arrays, together with the 2x2 swap matrix with rows (0,1) and (1,0).

known.name: Inner products, orthogonality and eigenvalues
known.gloss: The dot product of vectors, orthogonality when it vanishes, and eigenvalues and eigenvectors of a matrix as scalars and directions it only scales.

known.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
aliases: evaluate a polynomial at a point
known.gloss: Evaluating a polynomial at a value (in particular at a power of 2 to read it as an integer), and the idea that a polynomial of degree < N is determined by its values at N points.

known.name: Fixed-point and floating-point numbers
known.gloss: Representing real numbers as integers divided by a power of two (dyadic rationals), so p fractional bits give a grid of spacing 2^{-p} to which values are truncated or rounded, with rounding error below the spacing.

known.name: Karatsuba and the history of fast multiplication
known.gloss: The fact that integer multiplication can be done faster than the schoolbook quadratic time, so that the cost M(n) of multiplying n-bit integers is a nontrivial function studied in complexity theory.

known.name: Square roots and quotient with remainder
known.gloss: Division with remainder a = bq + r with 0 <= r < b, and the integer square root floor(sqrt(a)).
